A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

this report describes a novel case of diabetes due to a loss-of-function ABCC8  mutation previously known to cause congenital hyperinsulinism, highlighting the importance of genetic testing to achieve a proper diagnosis, and thus an adequate treatment, of diabetes.
this case report highlights the importance of genetic testing in the diagnosis of diabetes and its complications, as well as in the management of the disease.
the loss-of-function c.4058G > A (p.Arg1353His) ABCC8 mutation is associated with a diabetes phenotype and not with Congenital Hypersulinism as previously reported.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the genetic testing should always be performed in patients with unexplained diabetes, even when the clinical presentation is not typical of MODY.
genetic testing should be performed in all patients with diabetes and their family members to ensure appropriate treatment and avoid unnecessary insulin therapy.
genetic testing should be offered to all patients with diabetes, especially those who are young and have a family history of the disease.
